title: area
summary: Create filled area plots in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Documented GPU-array inputs execute on the client. RunMat additionally preserves compatible floating-point data on a GPU-backed geometry path; resident integer data gathers exactly before the graphics conversion.

description: `area` creates filled area plots from vector or matrix-style inputs. It returns one area handle per plotted series, supports baseline and stacked behaviors, and participates in the shared MATLAB/RunMat plotting handle-property system.
behaviors: `area(y)` uses implicit x-values `1:n`, while `area(x, y)` uses explicit x coordinates.
If explicit x-values are not increasing, each series is sorted by x before rendering; integer x-values are ordered in their native class before conversion to graphics coordinates.
Matrix-style `y` inputs create stacked area series in the MATLAB style.
Vector `y` returns one area handle, while matrix `y` returns a row vector with one handle for each column; every handle works with `get` and `set`.
Baseline and color workflows flow through the shared plotting property model.
All eight integer classes are accepted for X, Y, `BaseValue`, and `LineWidth`; integer plot data crosses one explicit client graphics conversion boundary.
Compatible floating stacked-series geometry can be emitted directly from GPU buffers on the RunMat acceleration path.
options: A positional numeric scalar or `'BaseValue'` name-value pair sets the baseline used by area filling.
`'LineWidth'` accepts a positive numeric scalar, including every integer class.
Color and display-name workflows are available through the returned handle and the shared plotting property path.

faqs.question: How do I create a stacked area chart?
How do I control the transparency of an area plot?
What's the difference between area and plot?
faqs.answer: `area` fills the region between the data line and the baseline, giving a visual sense of cumulative magnitude. `plot` just draws the line. Use `area` when the filled region conveys meaning—cumulative totals, part-to-whole breakdowns, or emphasizing the magnitude of a signal relative to a baseline.

gpu_residency: The documented GPU-array surface executes on the client, so resident integer X and Y gather with typed storage intact and convert only at the graphics boundary. RunMat preserves floating-point residency on a compatible direct path, including stacked-series geometry generation; other inputs use the semantics-preserving fallback.
gpu_behavior: The direct RunMat area path emits filled geometry from compatible floating GPU data when X is implicit or a known nondecreasing host vector.
Resident integer data and explicit resident X gather on the client so exact integer ordering and documented sorting occur before conversion.
Baseline semantics, stacked-series behavior, and one-handle-per-series output remain aligned across direct and fallback paths.
